description: We’re a team of 5 who love space and technology. Our strengths are coding, design, 3D, research and presenting. We’re curious, learn fast, and enjoy turning big ideas into things people can use and understand. We work openly, share tasks fairly and support each other. Join us to build, design and present, not just watch. We’re looking for someone with space science or NASA data knowledge, storytelling or writing skills, or testing experience. Reliable, curious people welcome.
summary:
HELIOS is an interactive web platform for exploring NASA’s SPHEREx infrared observations. It connects to the NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA) through the Simple Image Access 2 (SIA2) service, allowing users to search observations by sky position and selected filters.

Users can inspect FITS-based image previews and metadata, including observation time, detector, wavelength, and quality indicators. HELIOS supports visual comparison through blink, side-by-side, and image-wipe modes. It also offers an interactive 3D sky experience with WebXR support on compatible devices.

The platform separates live archive results, curated NASA imagery, and illustrative markers. Candidate markers are not verified discoveries, and HELIOS does not claim to have found Planet X. Its goal is to make SPHEREx data easier to explore and understand.
details:
HELIOS is an interactive platform designed to make NASA's SPHEREx observations easier to explore and understand. It provides a visual workflow that connects astronomical archive data with interactive exploration.

The Sky Explorer allows users to search SPHEREx observations using sky coordinates, search radius, collection, observation date, and detector filters. The application connects to the NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive through its SIA2 service and displays matching observation records.

Users can inspect FITS-based image previews and associated metadata, including observation timestamps, detector information, wavelengths, and quality indicators. The backend processes FITS data into browser-ready visual previews using image-stretching and shared-normalization techniques. These previews support visual exploration and comparison, not quantitative photometric measurements.

HELIOS provides three observation-comparison modes:

  • Blink comparison to switch between observations.
  • Side-by-side comparison to inspect observations simultaneously.
  • Image-wipe comparison to reveal differences between images.

The platform also includes curated NASA/JPL-Caltech SPHEREx imagery and an interactive 3D environment. WebXR enables immersive exploration on compatible browsers and devices, while desktop and mobile users can still access the main experience without XR hardware. Guided narration uses browser-native speech synthesis.

The project is intended for students, educators, astronomy enthusiasts, and members of the public. It aims to lower the barrier to exploring infrared astronomical observations by combining archive access, visual comparison, metadata, and immersive interaction.

HELIOS clearly distinguishes archive observations from curated educational imagery and illustrative candidate markers. Illustrative candidates are not verified astronomical discoveries. The project does not claim to have discovered Planet X.

Technology stack:

  • Frontend: React, TypeScript, Vite.
  • 3D and immersive experience: Three.js, React Three Fiber, React Three XR.
  • State management: Zustand.
  • Backend: Python and FastAPI.
  • Astronomical data processing: Astropy.
  • Testing: Playwright.
  • Data access: NASA/IPAC IRSA SIA2.

The main innovation is the combination of live SPHEREx archive exploration, FITS visualization, multi-mode observation comparison, and interactive 3D/WebXR experiences in one web platform, supported by transparent data provenance.
